0.1.unit: Vacuum distillation column T-101 separates 10 t/h of feed into crude acetic acid (top, 3.0 t/h) and acrylic acid (bottoms, 7.0 t/h) at 7.0 kPa a top, 89 °C bottom. The vacuum is made by a two-stage steam-ejector package: J-201 → surface intercondenser E-201 → J-202 → aftercondenser E-202 → vent; condensate drains by barometric legs to hotwell V-201. PIC-101 holds the column pressure by bleeding N2 into the J-201 suction (PV-201); the ejectors run at constant motive steam (PIC-210, 10 bar a).

rows.what: Column pressure creeping up: PIC-101 7.00 → 8.82 kPa a in 30 min
N2 bleed closed: FI-201 5.36 → 0 kg/h (LO alarm)

0.4.ctx: Afternoon shift on a hot day; unit lined out at design before the drift; no maintenance or set-point change logged. The tag snapshot at 0:30 compares every transmitter with its design value.

R.1.p: J-201 works on its curve: with critical flow its suction pressure rises in proportion to the gas and vapour it must move. That load is the air leak plus the N2 bleed plus whatever vapour the overhead condenser E-102 and the vent condenser E-103 let through, so warmer cooling water means more vapour and a higher suction pressure. PIC-101 keeps the pressure by trimming the N2 bleed: once the bleed is at zero the pressure is no longer controlled. The intercondenser sets the J-201 discharge (PI-202); the stage holds only while PI-202 stays below its maximum discharge pressure (MDP).

R.2.eq: W = Wd · (Ps − Pso) / (Pd − Pso)   (J-201 on its curve; it breaks if PI-202 > MDP)

5.1.proof: T-1 (utilities: CW hot), T-3 (TI-203 only −2.3 °C with 43 % more CW), Ev-11, Ev-12; WH-1 confirmed with it
5.1.mech: Two causes act together. (1) The CW supply warmed 30.0 → 38.0 °C (cooling-tower fans tripping) → every condenser warmer → E-102 and E-103 let more acid vapour through, TI-201 12.0 → 21.8 °C → more load on J-201. (2) E-201 is fouled: its approach widened 10.5 → 14.3 °C and its duty fell → PI-202 up. J-201 stays on its curve, so the extra load lifts its suction: PIC-101 trims the N2 bleed to zero (00:13:54) and then the pressure rises uncontrolled to 8.82 kPa a.

The bleed returned to 5.36 kg/h, its design value: the air leak is normal (WH-4 finally killed).

5.8.rule: When PIC-101 creeps up with the bleed at zero, compare the condenser approaches before you touch the ejectors.

evidence.text: PIC-101 rose from 7.00 to 8.82 kPa a in 30 min (a drift, steepest between 0:15 and 0:25); HI alarm at 00:14:59.
FI-201 N2 bleed fell from 5.36 to 0.00 kg/h (PIC-101 OUT 35.7 → 0.0 %); LO alarm at 00:13:54: the control margin is used up.
TI-110 cooling-water supply rose from 30.0 to 38.0 °C; HI alarm at 00:09:31, the first alarm of the case (TI-106 HI at 00:09:39).
TI-203 gas leaving E-201 rose from 49.4 to 59.9 °C (HI at 00:12:58); TI-204 CW return 38.9 → 45.6 °C.
TI-201 vent gas to J-201 rose from 12.0 to 21.8 °C (HI at 00:16:49).
Motive steam and second stage unchanged: FI-210 146.6 → 146.6 kg/h, PIC-210 10.00 → 10.00 bar a, PI-209 12.0 bar a, PI-203 110.0 → 110.0 kPa a.
TI-102 top temperature rose with the pressure, 48.0 → 52.9 °C (HI at later); PI-201 6.85 → 8.45 kPa a agrees with PIC-101.
Bottoms and product: TI-104 89.0 → 90.2 °C (alarm 95), AIT-107 0.50 → 0.59 wt% (alarm 1.0), distillate FI-103 3.00 → 2.80 t/h.
PI-202 (J-201 discharge) 25.7 → 27.6 kPa a; no J-201 or J-202 BREAK alarm in 30 min (the model's J-201 maximum discharge pressure went 29.7 → 33.0 kPa a, margin never below 2.5 kPa).
Snapshot 0:30: every set point and hand-controller output at its design value (PIC-101 SP 7.00, FIC-102 SP 1.655 t/h, HIC-102 80 %, HIC-201 70 %, HIC-205 70 %); LIC-201 hotwell 50.5 %.
Condenser approaches at 0:30 against design: E-201 TI-203 − TI-204 10.5 → 14.3 °C; E-202 TI-205 − TI-206 4.7 → 4.9 °C; E-102 CW rise TI-106 − TI-110 10.0 → 9.9 °C. Only E-201 got worse.
CW temperature rise across E-201, TI-204 − TI-110, fell 8.9 → 7.6 °C: at 2.4 t/h of CW the duty fell 25 → 21 kW. E-201 passes less heat, not less water.
Utilities (T-1, answer at 00:32:00): “MP steam header 12.0 bar a. CW supply 38.0 °C, the cooling tower fans are tripping. Chilled water normal. N2 normal.”

Field walk-round (T-2, 00:31:00): J-201 steady hiss; J-202 steady. Motive steam line dry. Vent clear, only a little vapour. Intercondenser shell warm. Column top 53 °C, bottoms 90 °C. Hotwell sight glass 50 %. CW return from E-201 46 °C. No hissing at flanges or sight glasses.

hyp.ifthen: If the CW supply is hot, then TI-110 is up and every water-cooled condenser (E-102, E-201, E-202) runs warmer by about the same amount; their approaches stay as they were.
hyp.fals: TI-110 normal, or utilities report the CW normal

hyp.ifthen: If the E-201 tubes are fouled, then its approach TI-203 − TI-204 widens while E-102 and E-202 keep theirs, it passes less heat, and more CW helps only a little.
hyp.fals: E-201 approach at its design value, or TI-203 back to design with more CW

hyp.cause: CW flow to E-201 low (HV-201, strainer)
hyp.ifthen: If E-201 is short of water, then the CW warms more across it (TI-204 − TI-110 up) and TI-203 rises.
hyp.fals: The CW rise across E-201 falls

hyp.ifthen: If more air leaks in, then PV-201 closes and PIC-101 rises while the condensers and TI-201 stay normal, and the field hears air drawn in at a flange or sight glass.
hyp.fals: No leak heard on the walk-round; bleed back to design once the cooling is restored

hyp.cause: J-201 motive steam weak (steam quality, nozzle, chest pressure)
hyp.ifthen: If J-201 gets weak motive steam, then FI-210 / PIC-210 / PI-209 move off design and PI-202 approaches the J-201 maximum discharge pressure: the stage breaks.
hyp.key: FI-210 or PIC-210 off design; BREAK alarm
hyp.fals: Motive steam at design and no break

hyp.cause: Second stage or vent restricted (J-202, E-202, FA-201)
hyp.ifthen: If the J-202 discharge is restricted, then PI-203 rises above 110 kPa a and PI-202 follows.

hyp.cause: PT-101 reads high (the column is really at 7 kPa a)
hyp.ifthen: If PT-101 reads high, then the real pressure is lower: TI-102 stays at its design temperature and PI-201 disagrees with PIC-101.
hyp.fals: TI-102 rises with PIC-101; PI-201 agrees

hyp.cause: Chilled water to the vent condenser E-103 lost
hyp.ifthen: If E-103 loses its chilled water, then TI-201 rises strongly and J-201 takes acid vapour; TI-110 and the other condensers stay normal; utilities report the chiller tripped.

hyp.cause: A set point or hand valve moved on the shift
hyp.ifthen: If somebody changed PIC-101 SP, FIC-102 or a CW hand controller, then the snapshot shows it off design.
hyp.key: SP / OUT off design in the snapshot
hyp.fals: Every SP and HIC output at design

hyp.ifthen: If the hotwell level is low, then the legs lose their seal and air enters E-201 / E-202: PI-202 and PI-203 rise and the field hears gurgling.

res.obs: TI-203 59.9 → 57.6 °C (−2.3), approach 14.3 → 13.9 °C (still far above 10.5); PI-202 27.62 → 26.07 kPa a; PIC-101 8.84 → 8.85 kPa a, no change: J-201 is on its curve, so a lower discharge pressure does not lower its suction.
